**Find, snip, cite — never rewrite.** The Fold finds a source, shows the source's OWN words (verbatim snip) under the creator's name with a link back, and does not paraphrase or retype content (recipes especially). Most asks need no model-written text at all.

**Two answer modes (user, 2026-10-05):** (1) *Facing page* — a model response drawn from snipped sources, shown beside them; (2) *Sources only* — the sources' verbatim snips strung together with citations, NO model call. **Never is it just the model talking:** a turn with no sources yields only an app-authored typed gap, never a model answer. Open question I raised: creative / code / transform / compute / smalltalk asks have no sources — interim behaviour is app-authored cards/notes behind a single `ALONE_KINDS` constant until the user decides.

**Tipping creators:** when content comes from a creator, offer to "tip the source" and say plainly it is a feature in development (the card's tip button only shows an 'in development, nothing sent' toast). The user then asked for an email-finder + `mailto:` outreach feature (find the author's contact on the page, "going to the IP owner if needed"). The auto-mode classifier blocked the first step as a real-world transaction; I did NOT build it and did not route around the block. If the user wants it: it must be user-initiated mailto only (nothing sent by the app), use only contacts the page itself publishes (never guess addresses, never use hosting-provider abuse contacts), and say where each address was found.

**n8n relay (`n8n.intelechia.com/webhook/feed`) is for TESTING only — never wire it into the app.** Measured as a search egress it was excellent (Brave page parsed 20/20, DDG 19/20) but the workflow has an SSRF hole (it fetched the n8n host's own `127.0.0.1:5678/healthz`); tell the user to add a private-address guard/allowlist/secret before anyone relies on it.

**Don't paste long copyrighted source text in replies**: describe snips by source/id; the app card shows them, my messages don't.

See [[chat-focus-and-search]], [[the-fold-naming]].

name: answer-pipeline-popper
description: "User's direction (2026-10-05) for factual answers: one answer + a citation, search that falsifies its own answer, a visible first-person reasoning trace; Popper-style falsifier runs gate every change"
metadata:

---

**An answer, not snippage.** For a factual ask the person wants "just an answer to my question with a citation, with the reasoning actually following good reasoning" — one realised line plus the source sentence verbatim, NOT a wall of passage blocks and never a small model's memory under a footnote ("we are too much trying to only answer by snippage").

**The search must falsify its own answer** ("the search ITSELF must falsify its answers"; Popper: "we can only asymptotically approach truth by falsification"). After a candidate exists, run a query that names the claim and ask "what could I find that would make me doubt it?" (death date, later holder, rival, negation). A claim ships only as "survived these named checks"; an unrunnable check is `unmeasured`, never a pass (Constitution II.10).

**Show the thinking, app-authored.** First-person plain-words trace ("it looks like a question of fact… I can't trust my memory, let me research… it says Charles III, let me falsify it…"), shown behind a disclosure; the void is stacked recursively (ask → referents → filler → currency → rival → falsify). Templates, never model text; no apparatus nouns/archon names on screen.

<pasted_content id="610a">
**Identity** is what a thing is for someone, not what it is in itself. Take everything the reading connects to a thing (what it touches, what happens around it, how that changes over time) and cut it off where the difference stops mattering. That cut-out neighborhood, seen from a particular perspective, is its identity. Two names are the same thing when their neighborhoods match under that cut, and when swapping one out for a generic stand-in disturbs the surroundings in the same way, by more than chance would. That is why identity is relative (it depends on the for-whom), revisable (more reading can move it), and earned (the thing has to carry weight, so idle things never count as the same).

**A definition** is that same fold written down in a portable phrase, by someone, so it can be carried and reused. "Faction" on its own is just a word, and Madison's sentence compresses what he wants it to mean into something that can travel. Live, reproducible: `node eval/origin/survey.mjs` and `node eval/origin/meaning-coverage.mjs` (they need the network; Wikipedia rate-limits — they wait and
retry). Predictions were not pre-registered for this first measurement; it is a baseline, appended to, never edited.

## 1. Does a Wikipedia sentence reach an origin? (`survey.mjs`, first 5 lead sentences of 6 articles, 30 sentences)
Articles: Marie Curie, Apollo 11, Nashville, Monarchy of the UK, Eiffel Tower, Charles III. Rungs 1 (consequence) only — no asker's frame.

| outcome | n | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| origin | 1 | a footnote's page was read and carries the claim (Marie Curie 1911 → nobelprize.org, address `origin#230-521`) |
| no-reference | 13 | the sentence stands under no footnote (leads seldom cite) — SIG, a refusal |
| unsupported | 11 | footnote pages were read and none carries the claim |
| unlocated | 3 | the extract's sentence could not be found in the article's markup |
| unread | 2 | every footnote page failed to read |

Why the 14 read pages did not support the claim (typed): `name` 3, `figure` 3, `unread-structure` (negation / comparison) 3, `terms` 2, `no-overlap` 2,
`cross-language` 1. Plus **7 footnote pages could not be read at all** (blocked, a PDF viewer shell, dead). So wording (`terms`, the paraphrase case) was
**2 of 14** — synonyms would have changed at most that.

## 2. How much synonymy does the reading's own hyperlexicon earn? (`meaning-coverage.mjs`, whole articles)
The relation reader (vendored khora `relations.js`, `minSurfaces: 2`) admits verbs by recurrence; two labels in one (end1, end2) slot is the only place a
synonym could be earned (the user's rule: same slot in equivalent claims).

| article | chars | verbs | notes | slots | slots with 2+ labels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marie Curie | 44,312 | 17 | 103 | 103 | 0 |
| Apollo 11 | 81,545 | 43 | 369 | 368 | 1 (`the\|area → landing, recovery`) |
| Nashville, Tennessee | 85,817 | 33 | 305 | 305 | 0 |
| Charles III | 68,509 | 32 | 247 | 246 | 1 (`was\|that → announced, reported`) |
| Monarchy of the UK | 60,049 | 31 | 267 | 265 | 2 (`monarch / king` — nouns, not synonyms) |
| Eiffel Tower | 44,988 | 15 | 97 | 97 | 0 |

On a lone claim plus one page the reader admits **0** verbs. **Measured null:** on a single turn the ledger earns essentially no synonymy; the pairs it
does find are not synonyms. The relation reader's own noise is visible (`physicist`, `family`, `station` admitted as "verbs"). Hence `fold-chat-meaning.js`
is built, tested on a hand-built ledger, and OFF unless a caller passes a ledger.

## What would change this
A corpus of real turns where a session-level ledger (many pages, many turns) earns pairs that the strict check then confirms; or a received synset prior
(`word-meaning.js` exists only in the legacy repos and would need migrating into khora — the user's call). The bound rung (frame) already sidesteps
verbs for slot asks. Re-run both scripts and append a dated section below.

Wikipedia is no longer cited anywhere in the chat. A Wikipedia sentence is followed to the page its own footnote names, that page is fetched and checked, and the path is kept. The full suite passes (1,491 tests, 0 failing, 1 existing `todo`), and I checked the Sources-only pointer rendering in the browser. Nothing is committed.

## How it works
- **Path:** the claim is found on Wikipedia, located in the article's own footnote markup, and the footnote's page is fetched (an archived copy only if the original can't be read). The path shows as *found via Wikipedia “X” → reference n → host*.
- **When it works:** the origin is cited as itself, with its own supporting sentence identified by address.
- **When it doesn't:** the Wikipedia words are drawn as "a pointer, not a source", with the pages it points at as links to fetch.
- **Surfaces changed:** the answer card, the Sources-only strand, the model's `[W#]` chips, the sources panel, and the attribution check ("according to Wikipedia" is now stripped). The disambiguation line stays, since it only offers Wikipedia titles as senses.
- **Not citing:** Wikipedia also never gets an "open ↗" or a tip button.

## Support check
This follows your definition of identity: each verdict names its cut and its for-whom, is marked `measured: false`, and a claim that carries too little is `undecidable`, never "same". There are three mechanical rungs, none using a model:
1. **Consequence:** the existing project rule, strict on wording.
2. **Pivot reading under the asker's frame:** `askFrame` and `bindSentence` read both sides into assertions. "Rises… runs" matches "flows", and a different filler or a denial is `different`.
3. **Hyperlexicon synonyms:** built but **off by default**, see below.

Your two operator tables are applied as data, not on screen. A refusal (SIG), a typed gap and a falsification (CON) are now kept apart, and each failure says its grain. A footnote page that says something else gives status `contradicted`. The trail also records how many pages carry the claim and how many distinct hosts they are, the article revision, and the date of any archived copy.

## Hyperlexicon synonyms: measured null
You chose "the reading's own ledger", so I vendored six khora organs with `--add`. On six real articles, two different verbs share a slot in only 0–3 of 97–368 slots, and the few that do aren't synonyms. On one claim plus one page the reader admits no verb at all.
- **Where it stands:** I built the mechanism with a guard against the claim and page vouching for each other, and left it off unless a caller passes a ledger.
- **How much it matters:** only 2 of 14 read-but-unsupported pages failed on wording. Names, figures, negations and unreadable pages dominate. Details are in `eval/origin/RESULTS.md`.

## What to know
- **Yield is low:** of 30 lead sentences, 1 reaches an origin, 13 have no footnote, and 7 footnote pages couldn't be read.
- **Pointer text:** an unresolved pointer still shows Wikipedia's words, labelled as such. Say if you'd rather show only the links.
- **Not built:**
  - recomputing composite claims (SYN);
  - a check for a term used outside its definition (DEF);
  - your substitution control for identity;
  - demoting a `contradicted` answer to a contest on the card (the trail already holds the refuting sentence).
- **Slot pipeline off by default:** the answer-card path only appears when `fold-chat:answerPipeline` is on.
- **Decisions I made:**
  - A claim may say less than the page's sentence, never something else. Your existing `sameClaim` is symmetric and rejected clauses of longer sentences.
  - I declared `minAtoms = 3` and following at most 3 sentences per passage; neither is measured.
  - I edited `scripts/vendor-khora.mjs` and the vendor pin, which already had your uncommitted changes.

The code is in `fold-chat-origin.js`, `fold-chat-originwire.js`, `fold-chat-tertiary.js` and `fold-chat-meaning.js`. I wrote `docs/ORIGIN.md` and saved your definitions to memory.
